text:
incident-bot: [P1] ALERT — High tail latency detected for redwood-3b (us-west-2). p99 > 6s for the last 5m, streaming stalls reported. Paging on-call.
linus_oncall: acked. I'm on it. pulling traces and traces-dashboard now.
eva_support: flagging customer-impact: a few enterprise tenants reported timeouts on streaming endpoints. CS notified.
ben_sre: any immediate rows in /metrics? can we see which hosts spike?
mike_runtime: checking serving-metrics. I see sustained GPU_util at ~98% on pool-gpu-03 and thermal trips on node gpu-03b. KV cache hit rate dropped 40% around the same time.
jia_mlinfra: ECC errors on gpu-03b in the last 15m per node-exporter: "ECC_UNCORRECTABLE=3". That matches stalls.
linus_oncall: steps: 1) divert new requests away from pool-gpu-03; 2) drain slow nodes; 3) open ticket with infra provider. executing now.
mike_runtime: updating routing policy, applying soft-fallback to redwood-3b-quantized on other pools to reduce GPU pressure.
ben_sre: drain command: `kubectl cordon node/gpu-03b && kubectl drain node/gpu-03b --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` — careful with long-running streams. I'll kick off canary fallback first.
linus_oncall: canary fallback rolled to 10% in us-west. tail latency reduced to p99 ~2.1s but p95 spikes persist.
eva_support: customers on tenancy ACME-Corp reported partial streaming stalls at 11:46 PDT. CS posted workaround to affected customers: reconnect stream or retry with exponential backoff.
mike_runtime: logs from runtime on gpu-03b: ``[2026-02-18T18:45:12Z] WARN StreamingStall: stalled 3.2s; last kernel error: cuMemAlloc: out of memory?; thermal_warning: 85C``
jia_mlinfra: node-exporter shows fan speed drops then rise; power capping events recorded. Looks like thermal throttling, not only ECC. ECC counts correlate with memory spikes.
linus_oncall: escalating to hardware: opening ticket with cloud provider referencing ECC/unrecoverable and TTR issues. attaching kernel logs.
ben_sre: while hardware responds, mitigation plan: 1) keep diverted traffic on other pools; 2) increase batch size tolerance on fallback to reduce token-level overhead; 3) temporarily lower default concurrency for streaming endpoints in us-west. Implementing 2/3 now.
mike_runtime: reduced streaming concurrency from 6 -> 3 for us-west router. That should reduce queueing.
linus_oncall: draining gpu-03b now; starting graceful migrate of KV caches and inflight requests.
eva_support: CS confirms 2 enterprise customers still see elevated latencies but no full outage. sending status update.
ben_sre: quick check: p99 dropped from 6.4s -> 2.3s after drains and routing changes. p95 down to ~700ms. Good but we need steady-state.
jia_mlinfra: provider replied: hardware team sees repeated ECC UCEs + evidence of thermal cycling. They recommended replacement and RMA for gpu-03b. ETA replacement 3h.
linus_oncall: schedule node replacement, mark as DO NOT SCHEDULE workloads until RMA. Also alert: check sibling nodes in same rack for early signs.
mike_runtime: enabling extra logging for stream stalls: `RUNTIME_LOG_LEVEL=debug RUNTIME_STREAM_SAMPLE=1%` — will capture stack trace for next 30m.
ben_sre: putting postmortem placeholders: impact window 18:44 -> 19:08 PDT, partial customer streaming stalls, SLO breach for p99 in us-west by ~+2.4s.
eva_support: sent customer status: "We are mitigating increased latency caused by hardware degradation in us-west. Fallbacks enabled; replacement in progress; we'll update in 1h."
linus_oncall: once RMA scheduled, we should run a full health sweep: NVML ECC counters, thermal history, power cap logs, BIOS firmware checks. Add a runbook entry for detecting early thermal cycling.
jia_mlinfra: agree. also add alert rule for sudden KV cache hit-rate drops coupled with GPU ECC increments -> will reduce time to detect similar issues.
mike_runtime: note: the quantized variant had slightly lower quality in a couple of requests — moving forward we should automate quality checks during forced fallbacks and run quick evals on sampled prompts.
ben_sre: at 19:02 PDT p99 stabilized to 1.9s. keeping monitoring for 30m.
linus_oncall: handoff to bench SRE for night watch: @ben_sre you're primary until RMA complete. I'll update on-call rota.
eva_support: final status update posted to customers and health page.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — traffic diverted, affected node cordoned, RMA scheduled. Severity P1 -> P2. Record created: INC-2026-0218-001.
linus_oncall: followups: - postmortem (owner: ben_sre) - runbook updates (owner: jia_mlinfra) - quantized-eval automation (owner: mike_runtime) - rack health audit (owner: linus_oncall). Please add timelines.
ben_sre: creating postmortem doc now and will include timeline, mitigation steps, and customer impact. ETA for draft: EOD today.
mike_runtime: will add logs and sample requests from the debug capture.
jia_mlinfra: will push alert changes to staging by tomorrow.
eva_support: I'll coordinate customer communications for SLAs and credits if needed.
linus_oncall: thanks team. re-open if p99 creeps again. :thumbsup:
